summary: Granite County tower on the Lolo National Forest, built 1934 with an L-4 cab; the cab was moved in 1949 as a maintenance cabin; tower gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com lists the tower as gone; the Weebly list marks it removed; the 1949 cab move is the only later event in the sources

events.note: Cab moved to T10N R5W section 25 NE as a maintenance cabin

evidence.supports: 1934 20-foot pole L-4 tower; 1949 cab moved to a maintenance cabin
evidence.quote: 1934: 20' pole L-4 tower. Cab moved to T10N R5W section 25 NE as a maintenance cabin in 1949.

evidence.supports: Granite County entry at 10N-14W-17 on the Lolo National Forest
L-4 is a standard 14 x 14 foot pre-cut house, built from 1929
evidence.quote: L-4 = standard 14 x 14 foot frame pre-cut lookout house built from 1929

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com places the moved cab at T10N R5W section 25 NE; the Forest Lookouts Granite County list places the Harvey Point entry at 10N-14W-17. The two township and range figures probably describe the tower and the cab's later site, but no source says so, so the story presents them as given.

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookout Tower Photos (lookout type definitions)

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one dedicated page, the Granite County list, and the statewide index. Two searches found no staffing, fire, or site-description sources. Brief coordinates (46.61505, -113.39605) were not checked against the township data beyond the Weebly entry. The moved cab's current status is unknown. Staffing omitted for lack of any source. No photos found.
